Probably one of my favorites on the list. The curriculum is solid, and I think the forums. Where you can actually find answers to the questions. And solutions to the problems, all really, really good. If you just go through from top to bottom,. You're gonna learn everything from HTML and CSS,. JavaScript, jQuery plugins. You're gonna learn APIs. And even a little bit of backend development. You're gonna learn how to think like a programmer,. Which is pretty awesome. Free Code Camp, absolutely love it. Once you've kind of gotten your wits about you. With HTML and CSS,. And you've taken some of those JavaScript courses,. You probably wanna learn by doing. And actually creating some projects. And Wes Boss has created an awesome program. Called JavaScript 30. It's absolutely free. It's 30 days of JavaScripts. Where you're gonna build drum machines. And all sorts of different applications. Using nothing but vanilla JavaScript,. And it's absolutely out of this world. He recommends that you have some sort of accountability buddy. So that you and somebody else can kind of program. At the same time and help each other out. Really great teacher, Wes Boss is pretty stupendous. Third is the website of Jen Simmons,. Specifically her lab.jensimmons.com. She's so stinking good and so smart. And she's a great teacher, Jen Simmons, all the way. Last one on the list is actually a fun little iOS app. And it's called Grasshopper. It's free to download and it's kinda like Duolingo for code. It just kind of has simple little levels. That you can kind of like run through. And hit each one of those levels. And then each day it'll actually push notify. And ask you one little question. And ask if you can solve that puzzle. So it's kind of like a constant thing,. Something just to kind of keep your mind on development,. Which I think is cool. So maybe check out Grasshopper. Next section is gonna be YouTube channels.
